summary: Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Vienna (~1958–1960) and completed his Promotion at Göttingen (~1960–1967). He later served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1982–2000).

Wilhelm Havers worked in linguistics and Indology. He held positions at the universities of Bern (~1915–1917), Leipzig (~1917–1920), Würzburg (~1920–1929), Breslau (~1929–1937), and Vienna (~1937–1953).

Wilhelm K. Essler is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1960–1966) under Wilhelm Britzelmayr and Wolfgang Stegmüller. He served as Director of the Institute for Philosophy at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1986–2006).

Wilhelm Max Müller worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1887) and the University of Leipzig (~1883–1888), and later held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1910–1919).

Wilhelm Pertsch worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, and at Berlin and Tübingen. His career included serving as librarian and director at Schloss Friedenstein and Forschungsbibliothek Gotha.
Wilhelm Printz was an Indologist who studied under Wilhelm Schulze (~1906–1911) and Heinrich Lüders (~1909–1911).

Wilhelm Rau worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig under Friedrich Weller and completed his Promotion at Marburg under Johannes Nobel. He held professorships at Goethe University Frankfurt (1955) and the University of Marburg (1958–1987).

Wilhelm Scherer worked in linguistics and literature. He studied at the University of Vienna and in Berlin under Moriz Haupt, Franz Bopp, and Karl Müllenhoff. He held professorships at Vienna (1868–1872), Strasbourg (1872), and Berlin (1877).

Wilhelm Schmidt worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893–1895) and later held positions at the University of Vienna (~1921–1938) and the University of Fribourg (~1939–1951).
Wilhelm Schott worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1823–1826) and later held a post there (~1838–1889).

Wilhelm Schulze worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Berlin and Greifswald under Johannes Schmidt, Heinrich Zimmer, and others. He held chairs at Marburg (1892), Göttingen (1895), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1932).
Wilhelm Solf was an Indologist who studied at Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, Kiel, Göttingen, and Jena. He held a post at Kiel University (~1887–1888).
Wilhelm Storck studied under Franz Bopp and Moriz Haupt.

Wilhelm Streitberg was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Münster, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held professorships at the universities of Fribourg (~1889–1898), Münster (1899), Munich (~1909–1920), and Leipzig (1920–1925).

Wilhelm Vatke was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Göttingen, and Berlin between ~1825 and ~1830, and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1834–1882).

Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1824–1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He later held a professorship at the University of Basel (1833; Ordinarius 1835–1869).

Wilhelm Wundt was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin (~1851–1856). He held posts at the University of Zurich (1857), the University of Leipzig (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena under teachers including Lichtenberg, Heyne, and Chézy. He served as a Prussian minister (~1819) and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1809–1810).

Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Lancaster University (~1990–1993) and the University of Cambridge (~1994–1999). He held a post at the University of Otago (~2003).

Will Tuladhar-Douglas works in religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, he directed the Scottish Centre for Himalayan Research, lectured at the University of Aberdeen, and is attested at the University of Hamburg (2026).
